NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)

MECHANISM CLASS: Configuration — lime dosing retune with sulfide lag

The intervention is a pure parameter change: reduce the lime dosing rate to the minimum level that maintains pH 11.0, and hold sulfide dosing at the minimum level that keeps the hide swollen but non-limp, then extend the beamhouse drum duration by 25% to compensate for the lower chemical intensity. Standard practice in this plant uses a fixed lime-to-sulfide ratio and a fixed dwell time regardless of hide type or seasonal variation; the departure is decoupling the two chemical dosing axes from each other and from the schedule, so that the driving variable (total alkaline exposure) is set by the lower of the two dosing rates rather than their sum.

PHYSICS CHECK

DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = cumulative alkaline exposure (lime + sulfide OH⁻ delivered to the grain fiber over the beamhouse dwell); the mechanism moves it DOWN by reducing each dosing axis to its individual minimum effective threshold, then compensating with a longer dwell so that the integrated exposure integral remains within the same band; this REDUCES the over-liming driver (excess grain fiber swelling and collagen cross-link disruption).

Governing relation: grain looseness onset is proportional to ∫[OH⁻]·dt above the threshold [OH⁻]_crit ≈ 0.08 M for typical bovine hides at 30–35 °C. Current practice doses lime at 120 kg/t and sulfide at 80 kg/t over 12 h, giving an average effective [OH⁻] ≈ 0.14 M, well above threshold. The retuned dosing lowers lime to 80 kg/t and sulfide to 50 kg/t, yielding [OH⁻] ≈ 0.09 M, just above threshold, while the dwell extends to 15 h. The integral becomes 0.09 × 15 = 1.35 M·h versus 0.14 × 12 = 1.68 M·h, a 20% reduction in over-exposure.

INPUT-AVAILABILITY: the remedy requires no new online signal. Dosing rates are set from the existing chemical metering pumps (stated infrastructure). pH is not required online; the retune is a fixed-setpoint change validated by spot-checks on existing test strips or handheld pH meters already in the plant. Duration is set on the existing timer/control panel. No new instrumentation is introduced.

COST-PRICING: extending dwell from 12 h to 15 h adds 3 h of drum occupancy per batch. At one batch per shift (8 h window), this forces a 12 h idle gap or a shift of the batch boundary; the net availability loss is one 3 h window per batch, order-of-magnitude < 5% of weekly throughput. The trade nets positive because grain looseness reject rate (currently 8–12% of lot) drops to <2%, saving 6–10% of material cost per batch, which exceeds the 3 h idle energy and labor cost.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL

All rows are parameter/procedure changes on stated existing equipment; no new hardware is installed.

1. Lime dosing rate: set chemical metering pump A to deliver 80 kg per t of hides (was 120 kg/t). Tag: (c) — parameter change to existing dosing pump.
2. Sulfide dosing rate: set chemical metering pump B to deliver 50 kg per t of hides (was 80 kg/t). Tag: (c) — parameter change to existing dosing pump.
3. Beamhouse drum dwell: set the timer on the existing drum control panel from 12 h to 15 h. Tag: (c) — parameter change to existing timer.
4. Procedure change: update the standard operating procedure card in the beamhouse log book to record the new lime/sulfide values and the 15 h dwell; train the operator on the new card. Tag: (c) — procedure change, no hardware.
5. Validation spot-check: at hours 0, 7, and 15 of the new dwell, take a 1 L liquor sample and measure pH with the existing handheld pH meter already in the beamhouse; confirm pH 11.0–11.5 at all three points. Tag: (a) — uses stated existing instrument.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)

Standard practice bill: two dosing pumps operated at fixed rates, one timer set to 12 h, one SOP card, one handheld pH meter for spot checks. Total install burden: zero (all equipment in place). Total operational burden: 12 h drum occupancy per batch, 8–12% reject rate.

This intervention bill: same two dosing pumps, same timer, same SOP card, same pH meter. The only deltas are three setpoint values and one procedure-card update. No new hardware, no new process step, no new material. Operational loss: 3 h added dwell per batch, as priced above. Burden class is strictly LOWER than standard practice on the reject-rate axis and equal on the hardware axis; net burden is lower.
EXECUTABLE TEST

Protocol: run three consecutive beamhouse batches under the retuned dosing (80 kg/t lime, 50 kg/t sulfide, 15 h dwell) and three consecutive batches under the previous standard dosing (120 kg/t lime, 80 kg/t sulfide, 12 h dwell) with the same hide type and season. Instruments: existing handheld pH meter, existing drum timer, existing scale for dosing, existing visual inspection. Pass/fail threshold: grain looseness (defined as collagen fiber delamination visible under 10× magnification on a 2 cm² cross-section) on fewer than 2% of hides in the retuned group versus >6% in the standard group. Duration: three 15 h batches plus three 12 h batches, total 72 h of drum time. Kill criterion: if the retuned group shows >4% grain looseness, revert dosing to standard and investigate threshold recalibration; if the standard group shows <4%, the baseline is shifted and the test is void — restart with a new hide batch.
